codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of per-component change detection using generation counters. The design is sound: SparseSet<EntityId, u64> per ComponentStorage tracks generations incremented on insert and get_mut. Type-erased AnyComponentStorage methods (max_generation, generation_for_entity) enable snapshot-based change tracking in ComponentStorageManager. The QueryChangedIter wrapper elegantly filters query results using a pre-computed HashSet of changed entity IDs. All 8 VAL-ECS assertions (013-020) plus an integration test for update() auto-clear are covered by unit tests. Code follows existing patterns and conventions.

issues.description: collect_changed_entity_ids iterates ALL entities with ANY component (via entities_with_components()), not just entities that have the queried component types. For worlds with many entities of different types, this is O(all_entities * queried_types) rather than O(entities_with_queried_types * queried_types). The correctness is fine because QueryChangedIter's inner query filters to only matching entities, but it means the pre-computed changed_ids HashSet may contain entities that don't match the query. This is a minor performance concern for large worlds, not a correctness issue.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The change detection design pattern (generation counters in SparseSet, snapshot-based comparison via max_generation) is a well-known ECS pattern (used by Bevy, Flecs). The existing pattern of code-generated-like repetitive implementations across iter1-iter8 is already established but worth noting for future workers who may add new arities.
